title: Optimal Complexity of Strong Pseudorandom Permutations
summary: Worst-case time proportional to t of N times log N is achieved; whether it is optimal for strong pseudorandom permutations on general sets given only efficient membership testing remains open.

formal_statement.body: $\Theta(t(N)\log N)$ is the optimal worst-case running time for strong pseudorandom permutations on general sets given only efficient membership testing.

scope.domain: Worst-case complexity of strong pseudorandom permutations on general sets using a cipher on a larger set.
assumptions: Membership in the target set can be tested efficiently.
A cipher is available on a larger set $T$.
parameters: $t(N)$: time required to encipher a point in the larger set $T$
$T$: larger set on which the available cipher operates
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or disprove that the achieved $\Theta(t(N)\log N)$ worst-case running time is optimal.

citations.label: Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications

progress.summary: The source reports a worst-case running time of Θ(t(N) log N), where t(N) is the time to encipher a point in the larger set T, and explicitly conjectures that this running time is optimal.
citation_labels: Sarah Miracle et al., Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications
